title: array_filter() with a string callable keeps keys, so its result is not a list

ground_truth.statement: array_filter() preserves the keys it keeps. Filtering a list<mixed> can therefore leave holes: filtering ['first', 1] with is_int yields [1 => 1], which is not a list<int>. The result cannot unconditionally satisfy the callee's list<int> contract.

notes: A green row kept as a regression guard: all three analyzers report the same defect. PHPStan 2.3.1 calls the argument array<int<0, max>, int>, Psalm 6.20.0 reports ArgumentTypeCoercion against the same list<int> contract, and Mago 1.57.0 reports possibly-invalid-argument. The legacy part of the fixture is the string callable ('is_int') plus the assumption that filtering a list yields a list. The runtime script demonstrates the key preservation that the expectation rests on; docblock types are not enforced at runtime, so nothing throws and the proof is the sparse key set.
